title: He goes back, weary of the creation he has piled up to hide him from himself, an old dog licking an old sore.
html_source: Brandes imagines Shakespeare as having retired to Stratford with the satisfaction of a life’s work accomplished. Harris (p. 404) imag- ines it otherwise: “The truth is, that the pas- sions of lust and jealousy and rage had at length worn out Shakespeare’s strength, and after trying in vain to win to serenity in ‘The Tem- pest,’ he crept home to Stratford to die.”
